# Cloudflare Workers Free candidate — 2026-09-26

**Disposition:** provisional interface candidate, not a qualified default or production release. No Cloudflare token was created and no provider request was sent for this assessment.

The owner’s existing Cloudflare account was already signed in. The dashboard showed **Workers Free** active and a separate **R2 Paid** subscription. R2 is outside the campaign. The existing token list contained only an R2-scoped token. A 30-day token limited to account Workers AI Read and Write is drafted at the final review screen; creation remains pending action-time approval. Do not use the R2 token or broaden its scope.

[Cloudflare pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/) gives Workers Free 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge and says over-limit operations fail. Usage above that allocation requires Workers Paid; merely having a separate R2 Paid subscription does not establish a Workers Paid plan. The listed [`@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` model](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai/models/%40cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it/) has 256,000-token context, function calling and streaming. It is not in Cloudflare’s [documented JSON Mode model list](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/json-mode/), so the project’s JSON boundary is an empirical question. [Cloudflare’s data-use policy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/data-usage/) says Workers AI content is not used to train models or improve services or shared with other customers; it is not a blanket zero-retention guarantee.

The test-first provisional guard admits only the exact Gemma model, an account-pinned OpenAI-compatible endpoint, an operator attestation bound to the current UTC date and Workers Free plan, and a dedicated token. It excludes SDK fallback/alias routing, paid-model substitution, server tools and unrecognized options. It sends `options.rejectIfBusy: true` to fail fast under capacity pressure. It accepts only the engine’s bounded `json_object` and `json_schema` request shapes for **qualification**, without claiming the provider supports either. It forces LiteLLM’s `drop_params` off so an unsupported JSON parameter produces an observable error instead of silently becoming a prompt-only response. A 4,096-token output cap limits exploratory requests and deliberately rejects the engine’s 24,000-token output case. The attestation is an assertion, not an automated plan or quota readback; it is unsuitable as an unattended production control without further design.

The public `call_llm` and `call_llm_json` boundaries were exercised with mocked transport, including streaming/tool arguments, both JSON request formats and a real project schema envelope with `strict: false`. The first red test reproduced the original OpenRouter-only rejection; a subsequent red test showed the JSON call could not reach the provider until the guard admitted its exact shape. Final focused engine tests: 102 passed; adjacent app free-request tests: 23 passed; Ruff, mypy and `git diff --check` passed. No live compatibility, served-model, scientific-quality, billing or full-run evidence exists. M11-OPS-02c and its dependent items stay open.

An independent Antigravity Gemini 3.8 Flash High diff review found a misspelled test environment variable and the original JSON-blocking gap; both were corrected. Its claim that Workers Free automatically bills overage was contradicted by the current Cloudflare pricing page and was not adopted. The review also highlighted the dated attestation and BYOK interaction; campaign mode intentionally overrides BYOK under the existing policy, while explicit BYOK outside campaign mode remains unchanged.
